title: Multiple instance learning for microscopy slide classification using unconventional staining techniques for bladder cancer screening
summary:
Background
Bladder cancer and cancer of the upper urinary tract are often diagnosed using an examination of the bladder and the analysis of tissue samples. These procedures can be burdensome for patients. Examining cells from urine samples is less burdensome, but it does not yet detect tumors reliably in all cases.

Research question
This study investigates whether artificial intelligence can reliably identify cancer cells or typical cellular changes in urine samples. It also examines which staining method is most suitable and whether collecting several samples at different time points improves detection.

Methods
Before a planned urological procedure, participants provide a urine sample. Some participants provide several samples. Slides are prepared from the samples, stained using different methods, digitized, and analyzed using artificial intelligence. The results are then compared with findings from tissue examination or endoscopic examination.
conditions: Urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder and upper urinary tract

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-age ≥ 18 years and ability to provide informed consent
-suspected urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder or upper urinary tract
-histologically confirmed urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder or upper urinary tract
-planned cystoscopic or endourological examination
-ability to provide at least one urine sample
Exclusion criteria:
-age < 18 years
-inability to provide informed consent
-inability to obtain a urine sample
